Bug_Title: Nm: Class defines equal(Object); should it be equals(Object)? (NM_BAD_EQUAL)
Bug_Details:
This class defines a method equal(Object).  This method does
not override the equals(Object) method in java.lang.Object,
which is probably what was intended. equal(Object) equals(Object) java.lang.Object
Bug_Explanation: The method 'equal(Object)' is defined instead of the standard 'equals(Object)' method. This does not override the 'equals(Object)' method from java.lang.Object as probably intended, causing potential logical errors if instances of this class are compared using 'equals()' method.
Trigger_Explanation: The test cases in the generated JUnit test class call the showBug method which in turn calls the wrongly implemented equal(Object) method instead of equals(Object). This leads to inconsistent results when comparing objects, as the standard Java equals method is not overridden.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that all tests passed successfully, which means the method 'equal(Object)' worked as expected in the context of the tests. This suggests that the presence of the method 'equal(Object)' instead of 'equals(Object)' did not cause any test failures, thus not confirming the bug triggering.
